newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: IMF SEES 1997 GDP GROWTH OF FOUR PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: IMF SEES 1997 GDP GROWTH OF FOUR PERCENT.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Monday that it expected Lithuania's economy to grow by around four percent in 1997 after expanding by around 3.6 percent last year.
"We would say that gross domestic product (GDP) in Lithuania will grow by four percent this year," Domenico Fanizza, the IMF's resident representative to Lithuania, told Reuters.
He added that the government had to continue structural reforms to sustain growth.
"The government has to stick to structural reforms, especially in the banking sector and privatisation," Fanizza said.

The Lithuanian government, headed by Gediminas Vagnorius, has vowed to complete the privatisation process launched during his first term of office in 1991 to 1992 and committed itself to shedding key state assets.
The central bank has taken significant steps to tighten regulations in the banking sector, which was rocked by a crisis in late 1995.
Lithuania's economy began growing again in 1994 after contracting sharply in the wake of the crack-up of the former Soviet Union, which severed the country's former trading ties and subsidies.
Preliminary data from the statistics department puts growth at 3.6 percent in 1996.
The government's forecast calls for GDP growth of five percent this year followed by an expansion of seven to eight percent in 1998.
